body:
**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

this is because reflection of "postgresql_where" is not supported right now in SQLAlchemy.   you should see a warning like this:

SAWarning: Predicate of partial index foo_idx ignored during reflection

As always, autogeneration detection via reflection is a partial process so you'll have to fill this in manually for now.

It appears that a string is not acceptable there.
When I replace the string with a comparison expression the migration applies successfully:

```
f2 = sa.Column('f2', sa.Enum('hurr', 'burr', 'something', name='sometable_f2_enum'), nullable=False)
op.create_table('sometable',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('f1', sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
    f2,
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
)
op.create_index('sometable_f1_f2_idx', 'sometable', ['f1', 'f2'], unique=True, postgresql_where=(f2 == 'something'))
```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

c7e5194dabde33e57532563, wraps text() around it.  obviously a pure SQL expression construct is best but there's no way SQLA is ever going to be able to render SQL expression constructs fully in reverse like that.

**Ulrich Petri ([@ulope](https://github.com/ulope)) wrote:**

Ah right didn't think of `text()`.

One last (I think) problem: the generated code tries to call `text()` globally but SQLA is imported as `sa` in the migration module - so it should be `sa.text()`

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

oh well there's a configured prefix, let me add that
